what: R6 training plan (docs/r6_plan_draft.md; user go 2026-11-09 'choose the best path and start compute'), sealed before any R6 training. One change from R5: the 399 OASIS-3 training heads of the sealed r6_oasis3_split (sha a02b3ce5...) are added. The user asked for a careful plan, a search for better choices and resource optimisation; the choices below and their reasons are fixed here so none is tuned on held-out data.
data: Dataset603_MRHeadR6 (headmodel.dataset.manifest_r6, head-model commit 6ac8357): R5's frozen manifest (data/manifests/r5.json: round 1 train + IXI train/val -> train; round 1 test + IXI test -> test, kept held out) + OASIS-3 train (399 finished charm runs; case02 dropped by the split rule: a 60 mm slab T1, 448x448x50 at 0.39x0.39x1.2 mm, that passed the selection script's slice-count check; its samseg hung) -> train; OASIS-3 test (100) -> test (imagesTs, never trained on, never predicted by this chain). Labels charm's tissue_labeling_upsampled on the T1 grid, as R5. Label QC before sealing (runs/r6/oasis3_label_qc.tsv): all 499 readable, no head-volume outlier, no class beyond 4 robust SD except two training heads at 4.1-4.5 SD on one bone class (kept); no head excluded.
segmenter: nnU-Net v2 2.8.1, 3d_fullres, default planner and plans, 5-fold split (seed 12345), all 5 folds, checkpoint_final of each, trainer nnUNetTrainerHMThick430 = R5's nnUNetTrainerHMThick (ThickSliceTransform p=0.3, k~U[2,6], gap as r5_train_plan_amend1) with num_epochs 430 instead of 250. Why 430: nnU-Net's epoch is 250 iterations, so R5's 250 epochs showed each of its 548 heads about 228 patches; with 947 heads, 430 epochs (947/548 x 250 = 432) keep that exposure per head, so the only difference from R5 is the data, not less training per head. Preprocess with 16 processes; 16 augmentation workers (nnUNet_n_proc_DA): the R5 run was GPU-bound (79 % GPU, 55 % CPU), so this only trims the data-loading share.
not_changed: Considered and not adopted for R6, to keep one change: (a) nnU-Net's residual-encoder presets (ResEncM fits the 8 GB clinic GPU: same patch 96x160x160 and features as the default on our data, deeper encoder; L and XL do not): run as a side experiment on fold 0 after the chain (scripts/r6_resenc_side.sh), compared on nnU-Net's own fold-0 validation, reported only; (b) a top-of-head crop augmentation: R5's 20 worst compare-set points are 16-60 mm from the image border (docs/r6_plan_draft.md), so there is no evidence for it; edge-touching input stays a locator hold; (c) SynthSeg-style domain randomisation (Billot 2023, PMID 36857946): a contrast-agnostic segmenter is PLAN 10.5 row C's job (phase 2), not R6.
warp: R6 warp net = warpnet.py's model and loss as R5 (rule r6_warp_train, sealed with this plan), trained on the out-of-fold predicted labels of every training head of Dataset603; validation = the 30 WP3b validation cases + the 30 IXI validation heads + 40 OASIS-3 validation heads (20 per stratum, the training participants with the smallest sha1('r6-oasis3-val:' + participant), fixed in the manifest before training).
rule: Nothing in this plan is changed after any R6 result is seen, except by a new sealed amendment that says why. The end-to-end rule r6_e2e (sealed with this plan) alone decides whether R6 replaces R5. The side experiment and the per-stratum numbers are reported and decide nothing.
no_folding: not judged here; r6_e2e states it (written-map min Jacobian > 0 on every test case of R6's 1 mm arm).
licence: OASIS-3 DUA: non-commercial, no redistribution, never off this machine, no face renderings. R6's weights are research models; whether they may be published openly or licensed needs OASIS's written agreement (docs/r6_plan_draft.md, point 1). R5 (CC BY-NC sources) stays the model for any release outside this machine until that is settled.
resources: RTX 5090 through resource_guard; estimates from R5's logs (29.2 s per epoch): preprocess ~2.5 h, 5 folds x 430 epochs ~17.5 h, out-of-fold labels + cache ~3 h, warp pilot ~4 h, final warp <= 7 h, scoring ~6 h with 3 cases in parallel (R5's sequential scoring used the GPU 22 % of the time); total ~40 h, about 17 kWh (GPU 405-445 W while training). Resumable at every step (nnU-Net checkpoint_latest --c; warp last.pt per epoch; e2e eval.json per run); scripts/resume_jobs.sh restarts the chains (the user installs the crontab).
